main_text.p: stotelem, nempe νεότης, ἀκμὴ[?] καὶ γῆρας, seu juventus, vigor, & senectus.
IuventusJuventus est ætas, in qua corpus animatum virium incrementum capit, propter auctionem calidi vitalis.
VigorVigor est ætas consistens, in qua corpus animatum plenas & integras vires est adeptū, propter vigore calidi vitalis.
SenectusSenectus est ætas, in qua corpus animatum, virium decrementū capit, propter diminutionem calidi vitalis.
MORSHactenus de vita: Sequitur Mors, quæ est interitus corporis viventis, factō[?] propter separationem animæ à corpore organico.
Genus mortis proximum statuitur inte-ritus seu corruptio substantialis. Mori enim est interire ac corrumpi. Ergo vi conjugatorum mors est interitus & corruptio.
Subjectum mortis est corpus vivens sive planta sive animal. Nihil enim naturaliter mori potest, nisi sit substantia composita ex anima & corpore organico.

Causa efficiens proxima & continens est separatio animæ à corpore organico: sive anima post separationem superstes maneat, ut hominis: sive simul cum toto composito destruatur, ut plantarum & brutorum.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the first word of the page's first line is a line-start fragment printed "stotelem" (long s rendered as plain s), probably "Aristotelem" with its opening letters cut off; left as printed. Greek accents in the first line are only partly legible; ἀκμὴ is marked [?]. "factō" is read from an abbreviated form and is uncertain. Left margin notes: Iuventus, Vigor, Senectus, MORS. Greek characters in the first line are copied as far as legible.
